stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्वपुर्नवकलायकोमलं
प्रेमदोहनमशेषमोहनम् ।
ब्रह्मतत्त्वपरचिन्मुदात्मकं
वीक्ष्य सम्मुमुहुरन्वहं स्त्रियः ॥ ५९-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna's form was beautiful and fresh like kalaya flower which radiated love and attracted the gopikas of the Brindavan day by day. They were captivated by His blissful form.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadvapurnavakalāyakomalaṃ
premadohanamaśeṣamohanam |
brahmatattvaparacinmudātmakaṃ
vīkṣya sammumuhuranvahaṃ striyaḥ || 59-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मन्मथोन्मथितमानसाः क्रमा-
-त्त्वद्विलोकनरतास्ततस्ततः ।
गोपिकास्तव न सेहिरे हरे
काननोपगतिमप्यहर्मुखे ॥ ५९-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Gopikas were so extremely fascinated with Krishna, that they longed to have His presence always and even the time He went to forest with the cows, it caused the pain of separation to them.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
manmathonmathitamānasāḥ kramā-
-ttvadvilokanaratāstatastataḥ |
gopikāstava na sehire hare
kānanopagatimapyaharmukhe || 59-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निर्गते भवति दत्तदृष्टय-
-स्त्वद्गतेन मनसा मृगेक्षणाः ।
वेणुनादमुपकर्ण्य दूरत-
-स्त्वद्विलासकथयाभिरेमिरे ॥ ५९-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Every morning after Krishna and Gopas left with their cows, Gopikas had their deer like eyes set in His direction. They listened to the sound of Krishna's flute from afar and continued to exchange stories about his pastimes with each other.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nirgate bhavati dattadṛṣṭaya-
-stvadgatena manasā mṛgekṣaṇāḥ |
veṇunādamupakarṇya dūrata-
-stvadvilāsakathayābhiremire || 59-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
काननान्तमितवान् भवानपि
स्निग्धपादपतले मनोरमे ।
व्यत्ययाकलितपादमास्थितः
प्रत्यपूरयत वेणुनालिकाम् ॥ ५९-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna after reaching forest, took shelter under the beautiful trees, stood cross legged and started to play His flute.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kānanāntamitavān bhavānapi
snigdhapādapatale manorame |
vyatyayākalitapādamāsthitaḥ
pratyapūrayata veṇunālikām || 59-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मारबाणधुतखेचरीकुलं
निर्विकारपशुपक्षिमण्डलम् ।
द्रावणं च दृषदामपि प्रभो
तावकं व्यजनि वेणुकूजितम् ॥ ५९-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The vibrating music from the flute attracted the celestial beauties. The cows and calves stood motionless. The birds on the trees forgot to chirp and melted even the stones.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mārabāṇadhutakhecarīkulaṃ
nirvikārapaśupakṣimaṇḍalam |
drāvaṇaṃ ca dṛṣadāmapi prabho
tāvakaṃ vyajani veṇukūjitam || 59-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
वेणुरन्ध्रतरलाङ्गुलीदलं
तालसञ्चलितपादपल्लवम् ।
तत् स्थितं तव परोक्षमप्यहो
संविचिन्त्य मुमुहुर्व्रजाङ्गनाः ॥ ५९-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s tender finger tips moved artfully on the stops of the flute, as Krishna kept tapping His tender feet rhythmically. The Gopikas visualised this pose in their minds again and again and got into a state of ecstasy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
veṇurandhrataralāṅgulīdalaṃ
tālasañcalitapādapallavam |
tat sthitaṃ tava parokṣamapyaho
saṃvicintya mumuhurvrajāṅganāḥ || 59-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निर्विशङ्कभवदङ्गदर्शिनीः
खेचरीः खगमृगान् पशूनपि ।
त्वत्पदप्रणयि काननं च ताः
धन्यधन्यमिति नन्वमानयन् ॥ ५९-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The celestial beauties, the birds, the animals and cows who were able to see Bhagwan’s form directly and even the forest which was always having contact with Bhagwan’s feet felt very lucky and blessed.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nirviśaṅkabhavadaṅgadarśinīḥ
khecarīḥ khagamṛgān paśūnapi |
tvatpadapraṇayi kānanaṃ ca tāḥ
dhanyadhanyamiti nanvamānayan || 59-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आपिबेयमधरामृतं कदा
वेणुभुक्तरसशेषमेकदा ।
दूरतो बत कृतं दुराशये-
-त्याकुला मुहुरिमाः समामुहन् ॥ ५९-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Gopikas felt sad and were in distress thinking when only they could get a chance to taste the nectar of Bhagwan’s lips which the flute was enjoying mostly as the flute was in contact with Krishna's lips most of the time.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
āpibeyamadharāmṛtaṃ kadā
veṇubhuktarasaśeṣamekadā |
dūrato bata kṛtaṃ durāśaye-
-tyākulā muhurimāḥ samāmuhan || 59-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रत्यहं च पुनरित्थमङ्गना-
-श्चित्तयोनिजनितादनुग्रहात् ।
बद्धरागविवशास्त्वयि प्रभो
नित्यमापुरिह कृत्यमूढताम् ॥ ५९-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Like this, everyday with the grace of Manmadhan, Gopikas were attracted to Krishna and this was actually a blessing for them, as they could keep their mind fixed on Him all the time though they forgot their household duties.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pratyahaṃ ca punaritthamaṅganā-
-ścittayonijanitādanugrahāt |
baddharāgavivaśāstvayi prabho
nityamāpuriha kṛtyamūḍhatām || 59-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
रागस्तावज्जायते हि स्वभावा-
-न्मोक्षोपायो यत्नतः स्यान्न वा स्यात् ।
तासां त्वेकं तद्वयं लब्धमासी-
-द्भाग्यं भाग्यं पाहि मां मारुतेश ॥ ५९-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Love or attachment comes naturally to every being but salvation can be obtained only by perseverance. For these Gopikas, their attachment to Bhagwan, helped them attain love and salvation together.
Wondering how fortunate they were, Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to cure him of his disease.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rāgastāvajjāyate hi svabhāvā-
-nmokṣopāyo yatnataḥ syānna vā syāt |
tāsāṃ tvekaṃ tadvayaṃ labdhamāsī-
-dbhāgyaṃ bhāgyaṃ pāhi māṃ māruteśa || 59-10 ||
